buckets.title: Surface Areas and Volumes
buckets.badge_reason: The central difficulty is choosing and coordinating surfaces or volume relations, not formula recall alone.

capabilities.action: Inventory present, absent, hidden and exposed surfaces before selecting area relations
capabilities.success_criterion: State exactly which physical surfaces contribute and exclude hidden/open faces with a reason

capabilities.action: Derive a needed slant length before applying cone surface area and coordinate it with exposure
capabilities.success_criterion: Use the axial right triangle for l and then apply only the exposed cone/solid surfaces

capabilities.success_criterion: Choose the correct invariant/ratio, preserve cubic units, and avoid solving unnecessary dimensions

grade9v3:component_waivers.EQUATIONS: The hidden-joint construction is a physical exposure decision; its useful bridge is the staged joint diagram and touch/paint test, not another equation card.

microtopics.title: Surface inventory before formula
microtopics.badge_reason: Open and joined solids punish formula-first reasoning.
entry_assumptions: Can find areas of circles and standard curved surfaces.
microtopics.inferential_jump: A surface-area expression must correspond to physical material that is present and included; open or internal faces contribute no exposed area.

teaching_path.action: List candidate surfaces before selecting a formula.
Mark each candidate present, absent, hidden or exposed.
Map each included surface to an area relation and add it once.
teaching_path.why_valid: The final area is a sum of the included physical pieces.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A named solid automatically implies its textbook total-surface-area formula.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does the top or joining disk physically exist as exposed material in this object?
misconceptions.repair: Inventory surfaces from the object/conditions first; choose formulas second.

exit_task.prompt: A closed cylinder is fixed to a flat circular plate of the same radius along one base. Which cylinder surfaces remain exposed? Explain before calculating.

answer.summary: The curved wall and the opposite circular base remain exposed; the attached base is hidden.
reasoning: The shared base is an internal contact surface.
Every other outer cylinder surface remains reachable.
answer.check: Use a touch/paint test on each surface.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task checks the surface inventory decision.

microtopics.research_contribution: Issue #18 question evidence clusters Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q7 around a surface-inventory-before-formula construction.

predict.prompt: When a container is open, should the missing opening contribute an area term?
predict.defensible_answer: No; an opening is not material.

accepted: Curved wall + existing base; no open top.
rejected: Use total surface area because the word cylinder appears.

task.prompt: For an open cylinder, list present surfaces and omitted surfaces.

route.ask: What physical material can you touch?
Which candidate face is missing or internal?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: The learner starts from a physical touch test instead of a formula list.

boundary_test.prompt: If the top is added, what changes in the inventory?
boundary_test.answer: One circular disk becomes present and exposed.
boundary_test.confirms: Open/closed status changes a surface term, not the cylinder's curved relation.

construction_units.decision: Decide what physical surface exists before choosing a formula

independent_checks.statement: CHECK: Name the surfaces of an open cylinder without calculating.
APPLY: Explain why a bowl mouth is not a circular material face.
CONNECT: Use the same inventory test when two solids are joined.

construction_units.decision: Remove internal joining faces from exposed surface area

independent_checks.statement: CHECK: Can paint reach a shared face after assembly?
APPLY: State whether one, two or zero copies of the joining disk belong in exposed area.
CONNECT: Distinguish exterior area from contact area in any composite solid.

compact_anchor.prompt: Open or hidden face? Inventory first.
compact_anchor.result: Only physical surfaces that are present and included contribute area.

microtopics.title: Auxiliary length before cone area
microtopics.badge_reason: The surface formula needs slant height even when the stem gives vertical height.
entry_assumptions: Can use Pythagoras in a right triangle.
microtopics.inferential_jump: The given height is not automatically the length required by the surface formula; derive the needed geometric quantity first.

teaching_path.action: Take an axial cross-section and label r, h and l.
teaching_path.why_valid: It reveals the right triangle embedded in the cone.

teaching_path.action: Use l²=r²+h² to derive slant height.
teaching_path.why_valid: The curved surface follows the sloping generator, not the vertical height.

teaching_path.action: Check l as the hypotenuse, then use πrl on the curved surface only.
teaching_path.why_valid: A plausible l and a surface inventory prevent height/base errors.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Use the vertical height directly in πrl.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Which segment actually lies along the cone's fabric?
misconceptions.repair: Locate l as the hypotenuse of the axial right triangle and derive it before area.

exit_task.prompt: A cone has r=5 and h=12. Without finding any surface area, identify the length the curved-area formula needs and explain how to obtain it.

answer.summary: It needs slant height l, found from l²=5²+12².
reasoning: The curved surface follows the sloping side.
The axial cross-section makes l the hypotenuse.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task assesses route selection before arithmetic.

microtopics.research_contribution: Q4 and Q6 repeatedly require a geometry bridge before mensuration.

predict.prompt: Does πrl use vertical height h?
predict.defensible_answer: No; it uses slant height l.

attempt.produces: A labelled axial triangle and a slant-height relation.

rubric.evidence_of: Selects the correct length for curved area.

accepted: Use Pythagoras on r, h, l first.

task.prompt: Label r, h and l on the cone cross-section.

route.ask: Which segment is on the surface?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Starts from the formula's required symbol and works backward to the geometry.

boundary_test.prompt: If l is already given, is Pythagoras necessary?
boundary_test.answer: No; use the supplied l after checking the surface condition.
boundary_test.confirms: The bridge is conditional on missing slant height.

construction_units.decision: Derive the length the surface relation needs before calculating area

independent_checks.statement: CHECK: Which of h or l lies on the curved surface?
APPLY: Draw the right triangle for r, h and l.
CONNECT: Use the derived l only after deciding which cone surfaces are exposed.

compact_anchor.prompt: Surface formula asks for l but the stem gives h.
compact_anchor.result: Build the axial triangle and derive l first.

grade9v3:component_waivers.STAGED_VISUAL: The decisive construction is symbolic/contextual: distinguish capacity, conserved volume and a shared formula factor. A decorative solid drawing adds no semantic bridge for this competition learner.

microtopics.title: Volume as capacity, invariant and shared factor
microtopics.badge_reason: The learner must decide what role volume plays before calculating.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate standard solid volumes and convert m³ to litres.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Volume is not just a formula result: it can represent capacity, conserved material amount, or a shared factor whose ratio avoids unnecessary unknowns.

teaching_path.action: Name the role volume plays in the context.
teaching_path.why_valid: This determines whether to convert, conserve, or compare.

teaching_path.action: Apply the matching volume relation while preserving cubic scaling.
Reverse-convert or use a dimensionless ratio to check.
teaching_path.why_valid: A second route catches unit and scale errors.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Treat recasting as surface-area conservation or use a linear scale ratio for volume.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: What physical quantity measures the amount of metal?
misconceptions.repair: No material loss conserves volume; similar-solid volume scales with the cube of the linear scale.

exit_task.prompt: A cylinder and cone have equal base radius and height. Without solving r or h, compare their volumes and explain the common factor.

answer.summary: The cone has one third of the cylinder's volume.
reasoning: Both contain the common factor πr²h.
answer.check: Multiply the cone volume by 3 to recover the cylinder volume.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task checks structural formula comparison.

microtopics.research_contribution: Q8-Q10 show three uses of volume that should be connected rather than taught as isolated formulas.

predict.prompt: When a solid is melted without loss, which quantity must stay the same?
predict.defensible_answer: Volume, because the amount of material is unchanged.

attempt.produces: A choice among conversion, conservation and ratio reasoning.

rubric.criterion: Names the correct role of volume before calculating.
rubric.evidence_of: Chooses the governing model rather than a surface/linear substitute.

task.prompt: For capacity, recasting and equal-r/h comparison, name what volume is doing in each case.

route.ask: Is the question asking how much fits, how much material remains, or how two formulas compare?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Starts from context language and maps it to the invariant/operation.

boundary_test.prompt: Is surface area conserved when one sphere becomes many smaller spheres?
boundary_test.answer: No; new boundary surface is created although volume is conserved.
boundary_test.confirms: Conservation applies to material volume, not boundary area.

construction_units.decision: Choose what volume means in the problem before performing arithmetic

independent_checks.statement: CHECK: State 1 m³ in litres and explain why this is a volume conversion.
APPLY: For a 3:1 radius ratio of spheres, state the volume ratio.
CONNECT: Compare cone and cylinder formulas by cancelling their common πr²h factor.

compact_anchor.result: Choose the role of volume first; then convert, conserve or take a ratio.

relations.expression: required area = sum of the areas of physical surfaces that are present and included
relations.meaning: Surface-area modelling starts with a physical surface inventory; a missing opening or hidden interface contributes no exposed area.
conditions: Count each included physical surface once.
Do not add an open face or an internal joining face.

derivation.action: Name every physical surface before writing a formula.
derivation.why_valid: A formula can only be chosen after the geometry has been interpreted.

derivation.action: Map each included surface to its 2D area relation.
derivation.why_valid: A 3D surface-area result is a sum of 2D areas.

derivation.action: Check each term against a surface that can physically be pointed to.
derivation.why_valid: This catches missing, duplicate and hidden faces.

limits: The rule does not decide whether a real container has thickness; the question's model does.
checks: Point to one physical surface for every area term and one reason for every omitted candidate face.

relations.expression: l² = r² + h²; curved cone area = πrl
relations.meaning: A cone's curved surface uses slant height l, so a problem that gives only vertical height h may require a geometry step first.
conditions: The axial radius and vertical height form a right angle.

derivation.action: Take an axial cross-section and locate r, h and l.
derivation.why_valid: The cross-section exposes the right triangle that governs slant height.

derivation.action: Use Pythagoras to obtain l before surface area.
derivation.why_valid: The curved-area relation requires l rather than h.

derivation.action: Check that l is longer than both r and h before using πrl.
derivation.why_valid: The hypotenuse must be the longest side.

limits: Do not use h in place of l in πrl.
checks: Substitute the derived l back into l²=r²+h².

relations.expression: volume measures occupied capacity; no-material-loss recasting conserves volume; for equal r and h, V_cone = V_cylinder/3
relations.meaning: The same volume idea supports unit conversion, conservation under recasting, and structural comparison of formula factors.
conditions: Capacity conversion preserves the same physical volume.
Recasting conservation assumes no material is lost.
The cone/cylinder one-third relation requires equal radius and height.

derivation.action: Identify what volume means in the question: capacity, material amount, or a formula factor.
derivation.why_valid: Different contexts use the same quantity for different reasoning jobs.

derivation.action: Preserve cubic scaling and units while applying the relevant relation.
derivation.why_valid: Volume scales with three linear dimensions and must retain cubic meaning until a valid capacity conversion.

derivation.action: Use a ratio or reverse conversion to check the result.
derivation.why_valid: An independent ratio exposes unit or scaling mistakes.

limits: Surface area is not generally conserved when a solid is divided or recast.
checks: Reverse the unit conversion or compare the relevant formula ratio.

question_families.title: Surface inventory and area selection
solution_structure: Map surfaces to area relations and add once.

demand_dimensions.model_choice: Choose which surfaces and relations actually apply.
demand_dimensions.representation_translation: Translate a 3D object or verbal condition into 2D surface terms.
demand_dimensions.reasoning_steps: Inventory, bridge if needed, calculate, check.

safe_variations: Change dimensions while preserving the same surface condition.
transfer_boundaries: Do not infer material thickness or lids that the stem does not state.
common_wrong_routes: Select a memorized total-surface-area formula before inventorying surfaces.

question_families.title: Volume as capacity, invariant and structural ratio
solution_structure: Apply the volume relation or invariant.
Preserve cubic scaling/units and verify by ratio.

demand_dimensions.model_choice: Choose capacity conversion, conservation, or structural formula comparison.
demand_dimensions.representation_translation: Translate words such as filled or recast into volume operations.
demand_dimensions.novelty: Same quantity used in three distinct reasoning contexts.

safe_variations: Change fill fraction, scale ratio, or common cylinder volume.
transfer_boundaries: No-material-loss is required for recasting conservation.
common_wrong_routes: Use surface area or a linear scale where a cubic quantity is required.
